articles.originalTitle: Ursula von Rydingsvard, Sculptor of Gigantic Cedar Forms, Dies at 84 - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ursula von Rydingsvard, Sculptor of Monumental Cedar Forms, Dies at 84
articles.excerpt: Ursula von Rydingsvard, a sculptor known for her monumental cedar works that challenged Minimalism with a human touch, has died in New York at the age of 84 following a battle with Alzheimer’s disease.
articles.content: Ursula von Rydingsvard, a sculptor celebrated for her towering, undulating works crafted from cedar beams in defiance of Minimalism's cold aesthetic, has died in New York at the age of 84. Born in Germany to displaced peasant parents and raised in Connecticut under blue-collar conditions, she pursued her education at Columbia University before establishing her career in New York. Mary Sabbatino, vice president and partner at Galerie Lelong, noted that her monumental sculptures stand as sentinels to inspire new generations. Her works have been exhibited widely, from the Storm King Art Center to the Yorkshire Sculpture Park. In 2013, she premiered Ona at Brooklyn’s Barclay Center, a 12,000-pound, 19-foot-tall cedar installation. While working primarily with standard 4x4 cedar beams to evoke earthy and biological forms, she also integrated materials such as silk, hair, and cow intestines into her large-scale pieces. Throughout her career, she maintained a strong desire for the permanence and proper preservation of her intricate sculptures.

articles.originalTitle: Tatiana Trouvé’s Art Is All About Getting Lost and Found and Lost Again - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Tatiana Trouvé Exhibits Works at Xavier Hufkens Gallery in Brussels
articles.excerpt: Artist Tatiana Trouvé is presenting her first exhibition with Brussels-based gallery Xavier Hufkens, featuring a mix of sculptures, drawings, and installations across three floors through October 31.
articles.content: Artist Tatiana Trouvé is showcasing a combination of sculptures, drawings, and installations in her first exhibition with Brussels-based gallery Xavier Hufkens, on view through October 31 across all three gallery floors. The opening room features L'inventario, an installation displaying various studio materials cast in metal and stone upon bronze cardboard shelves. The exhibition also includes abstract diagrams rendered in black cast iron and plaster that track noise pollution on the outskirts of Paris. Trouvé employs a process involving bleach poured onto industrial colored paper to build her cosmic-style drawings without complete control over the medium. Influenced by her upbringing in Senegal and local traditions, her works emphasize human presence through absence. Pieces such as her Guardian series, inspired by museum security guard chairs, and Sitting Sculptures, which combine stone with bronze casts of foam padding, reflect this thematic approach. The installations and objects on display incorporate traces of movement and suggest an independent life for inanimate forms.

articles.originalTitle: Michele Bönan Has Been Designing Hotels for Over 50 Years. And Is Still at the Top of His Game - WWD
articles.title: Architect Michele Bönan Reflects on Five Decades of Design
articles.excerpt: Italian architect Michele Bönan reflects on a career spanning nearly 50 years, designing refined residential-style hotels while noting that modern luxury centers on wellness and privacy.
articles.content: Florence-based architect Michele Bönan transforms grand palaces and boutique hotels into intimate spaces through an eclectic blend of Italian craftsmanship, antiques, and bespoke furnishings. Over a career spanning nearly 50 years, Bönan has collaborated with brands including Rocco Forte Hotels, Lungarno Collection, and J.K. Place. He observes that contemporary luxury has evolved, with guests increasingly prioritizing wellness, privacy, and a sense of belonging over impersonal grandeur. Bönan began designing while still at university, launching his professional path in the 1980s. His residential-style approach is exemplified by projects such as Casa J.K. Place Roma Residences, set within an 18th-century Roman palazzo featuring bronzed-steel kitchens, Calacatta marble, and historic salvaged fireplaces. Bönan is currently working on transforming the historic Palazzo dei Principi Caravita di Sirignano in Naples, with the property slated to open in 2027 to offer visitors the experience of staying in a noble residence.

articles.originalTitle: Morphosis and Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates Reveal Design of Campus Expansion at the Perot Museum - Architectural Record
articles.title: Expansion Plans Revealed for Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas
articles.excerpt: Morphosis and Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates revealed plans to transform a 4-acre area around the Perot Museum in Dallas into an outdoor science center.
articles.content: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas announced plans to transform 4 acres of surface parking surrounding its building into an outdoor science destination featuring interactive exhibits and planted landscapes. Morphosis, designer of the original museum building, is leading the project alongside landscape architect Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates. Spanning approximately 60,000 square feet, the expansion will feature interconnected zones with about 25 large-scale exhibits and 40 learning stations exploring natural forces such as wind, water, and weather. Planned attractions include a fire tornado, a giant water vortex, a cloud maze, and projects demonstrating wind and moving water effects. Shade trees, native plantings, and water features will integrate the landscape into the educational experience to introduce biodiversity. The project also includes a redesigned entrance, expanded dining and event spaces, a new parking garage, and infrastructure improvements. The expansion is part of the museum's $185 million Curiosity Unbound capital campaign. Construction is expected to start in early 2027 and reach completion in late 2028.

articles.originalTitle: John Ronan Architects Transforms a Manufacturing Facility Into an Architecture Hub for the University of Michigan - Architectural Record
articles.title: John Ronan Architects Transforms a Manufacturing Facility Into an Architecture Hub for the University of Michigan
articles.excerpt: John Ronan Architects has converted a 1930s-era former manufacturing facility into Liberty Annex, a new research and exhibition hub for the University of Michigan Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning.
articles.content: To accommodate a growing student enrollment and expanding academic programs, the University of Michigan Taubman College of Architecture and Urban Planning opened Liberty Annex as a new satellite facility in downtown Ann Arbor. Chicago-based John Ronan Architects converted a former manufacturing facility along West Liberty Street into a 19,000-square-foot space featuring student workspaces, faculty offices, and a public exhibition gallery. Because the building is historically protected, exterior alterations were disallowed, prompting the design team to execute all modifications internally. The architects introduced a mezzanine level and utilized hot-rolled steel elements to accommodate a multi-purpose program while maintaining the structure's original industrial character. Interior brickwork was sandbasted and concrete floors were ground down and polished during the conversion. The soaring double-height exhibition space serves as the public-facing centerpiece of the facility, currently hosting an inaugural exhibition dedicated to the works of the design firm.

articles.originalTitle: Frieze London 2026 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze London 2026 Opens with Greater Global South Representation and New Fair Additions
articles.excerpt: The Frieze London 2026 art fair has drawn attention with increased representation from the Global South, new cultural districts, and related events, while broader industry shifts and institutional developments continue to unfold.
articles.content: The Frieze London art events highlight an increased representation of galleries from the Global South, North Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia, particularly within the Frieze Masters section. Ahead of the inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi, a new cultural district named Noma has been announced near Saadiyat Island. Meanwhile, administrative disputes and restructuring at Goldsmiths have led to a student strike lasting 130 days. Regulatory changes are also impacting the sector, as the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation requires galleries and museums to improve and report on packaging sustainability. Okiki Akinfe won the inaugural £30,000 emerging artist prize funded by the Dasha Shenkman Focus Fund, while Theo Triantafyllidis presented a spider sculpture featuring a multiplayer video game at the fair. Additionally, various exhibitions across London continue to juxtapose historical works with contemporary installations.

articles.originalTitle: Jogen Chowdhury, ‘Towering Pillar’ of Indian Modern Art, Has Died at 87 - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Jogen Chowdhury, Leading Figure in Modern Indian Art, Dies at 87
articles.excerpt: Jogen Chowdhury, one of India's leading modern painters, has died at a hospital in Kolkata at the age of 87, drawing widespread tributes from the cultural community.
articles.content: Jogen Chowdhury, one of India's leading modern painters whose figurative oeuvre focused on humanity, died at a hospital in Kolkata at the age of 87. Indian media reports indicated that he had been suffering from a rare blood cancer for over a year. Cultural figures, including West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and Kolkata-based painter Samir Aich, paid tribute to his artistic legacy and association with the Bengal School of Art. Born in 1939 in Faridpur, Chowdhury trained at the Government College of Art & Craft in Kolkata and later at the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris. Renowned for his distinct line work and cross-hatching technique to visualize psychic interiors through distorted human figures, he exhibited internationally and received honors such as the Prix de la Jeune Peinture in Paris, the Kalidas Samman, and the Banga Bibhushan civilian award. Alongside his artistic career, Chowdhury served as a curator at Rashtrapati Bhavan and was a member of India's Rajya Sabha from 2014 to 2020.

articles.originalTitle: Unique collection of historic Anglo-Indian artworks gifted to Tate by Charles Greig – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Charles Greig Gifts 18th and 19th-Century Anglo-Indian Artworks to Tate
articles.excerpt: Art historian Charles Greig has donated a collection of 50 artworks dating from the 18th and 19th centuries to Tate. The works will be displayed at Tate Britain in 2028.
articles.content: Tate has received a collection of 50 artworks from the 18th and 19th centuries, donated outright by art historian and scholar Charles Greig. Gifted without tax incentives, the collection comprises oil paintings, watercolours, and miniatures that reflect the cultural and political changes during British colonialism in South Asia. Assembled over four decades, the collection features works by Indian artists such as Sita Ram and Ghulam Ali Khan, alongside European creators including Johan Zoffany, Rudolph Swoboda, William Hodges, and the Daniell brothers. Key highlights include Johan Zoffany's 1784 portrait of Prince Jawan Bakht and Rudolph Swoboda's Sepoy painting, introducing Company paintings to Tate's holdings for the first time. Tate Britain Director Alex Farquharson noted that the acquisition strengthens the museum's representation of art from the British Empire. Charles Greig expressed satisfaction in ensuring the collection remains preserved and accessible to the public. The works will be exhibited for the first time in a dedicated free display at Tate Britain in 2028.

articles.originalTitle: TATE ACQUIRES NEW WORKS FOR THE UNIQUE COLLECTION OF HISTORIC ANGLO-INDIAN ARTWORKS GIFTED TO TATE BY CHARLES GREIG – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Acquires an Exceptional Collection of 50 Historic Anglo-Indian Artworks
articles.excerpt: Art historian Charles Greig has gifted 50 18th and 19th-century Anglo-Indian artworks to Tate, with a dedicated public display planned for 2028.
articles.content: Tate has received a collection of 50 artworks by artists who lived and worked in India during the 18th and 19th centuries, gifted outright by art historian Charles Greig. Made without tax incentives, the philanthropic donation reflects the cultural, social, and political changes brought by British colonialism in South Asia. Greig's collection comprises oil paintings, watercolours, and miniatures built over four decades. It features works by Indian artists such as Sita Ram and Ghulam Ali Khan alongside European and British artists like Johan Zoffany, Rudolf Swoboda, William Hodges, Thomas Daniell, and William Daniell. Key highlights include Zoffany's 1784 portrait of Prince Jawan Bakht, Swoboda's c.1886 Sepoy portrait, and three watercolours by Sita Ram. Tate Britain Director Alex Farquharson noted that the gift will strengthen holdings of art produced in the British Empire. The public will first see the works in 2028 at a dedicated free display at Tate Britain.

articles.originalTitle: Agata Bogacka’s Tortured Symbolism - ArtReview
articles.title: Agata Bogacka's Abstract Paintings Examine Political Triumphs and Societal Divisions
articles.excerpt: Polish artist Agata Bogacka presents a series of abstract paintings exploring political transitions, societal divisions, and identity debates through sweeping, pastel-toned color gradations.
articles.content: Agata Bogacka's recent exhibition explores political transitions in Poland from communist totalitarianism to free-market democracy, alongside ongoing debates surrounding LGBTQ rights. Displayed at Edel Assanti in London, the suite of 2026 paintings features sweeping pastel-toned strokes applied with an exceptionally wide brush, intended by the artist to symbolize the political spectrum. Works titled under the series "Interactionship" include pieces like Disagreement, Annexation, and Equality Dream 11 and 12, which integrate elements of the rainbow flag into abstract-expressionist structures. The symmetrical diptych Avoidants 7 & 8 branches into conceptual sculpture territory, utilizing a downward-moving swath of pink lines and central voids to suggest unbridgeable gaps between ideological poles. Meanwhile, the Declarations series employs A4-paper-sized rectangular forms floating over bare canvas to reference empty political promises, contrasting societal discord with soft, accessible aesthetics.

articles.originalTitle: Brand new museums deserve brand new approaches to wayfinding with Fieldwork Facility - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sustainable Wayfinding and Signage Approach for V&A East Sites
articles.excerpt: Design studio Fieldwork Facility developed a modular, lower-impact wayfinding and signage system across V&A East Storehouse, the David Bowie Centre, and V&A East Museum to reduce environmental impact.
articles.content: Working across the V&A East Storehouse, David Bowie Centre, and V&A East Museum, Hackney-based design studio Fieldwork Facility combined creative design with sustainability strategies to reduce the environmental impact of wayfinding, labelling, and interpretation. The studio utilized lower-impact materials designed to minimise waste and maximise reuse through a modular system where signs can be disassembled, updated, and recycled. At V&A East Storehouse, primary signage utilizes recycled composite paper blocks, recycled plastics for lettering, aluminium cases, and enameled lava-stone roundels. V&A East Museum features a distinct style combining European sycamore wood instead of imported bamboo to lower shipping emissions, alongside recycled plastics. To address the widespread museum challenge of single-use plastic vinyl graphics, Fieldwork Facility painted graphics directly onto walls and created 1,240 hand-finished tiles from wood and recycled plastics for temporary exhibitions. Narrow scrolling LED ticker displays were additionally introduced for real-time event information. Despite extensive efforts to eliminate single-use vinyl, approximately 6 square meters of vinyl was retained exclusively for booking QR codes.

articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Exhibition Explores the Origins of Art Photography
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is hosting Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, an exhibition exploring pictorialism. The showcase features over 200 rare vintage prints and runs through February 2027.
articles.content: Tate Modern is hosting a major exhibition titled Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, which examines pictorialism, the first international art photography movement. Running from 14 October 2026 to 21 February 2027, the exhibition brings together over 200 rare vintage photographic prints from around the world. Beginning in the 1880s, pictorialist photographers sought to establish photography as a genuine art form comparable to painting, employing imaginative darkroom techniques and expressive compositions. The showcase highlights diverse analogue processes, including platinum prints, bromoil prints, and photogravures, alongside a functioning darkroom where visitors can learn environmentally friendly developing techniques on select days. Featured creators include Alvin Langdon Coburn, Soichi Sunami, and members of the Brazilian group Foto Cine Clube Bandeirante, who expanded the movement's modernist possibilities across decades. Tickets are available for purchase, and admission is free for museum members, who can also access a smartphone audio guide.

articles.originalTitle: Stefano Boeri Architetti to transform industrial site into residential neighbourhood in Tbilisi - Dezeen
articles.title: Former Soviet Factory in Tbilisi to Be Transformed into Residential Neighbourhood
articles.excerpt: Stefano Boeri Architetti will redesign a former Soviet locomotive factory in Tbilisi as part of the Loco Park master plan, incorporating housing, green spaces, and community areas.
articles.content: Italian studio Stefano Boeri Architetti has revealed plans to overhaul a former factory on an industrial site in Tbilisi. Having won the competition to design the Loco Park master plan, which will add housing, green spaces, and community areas to the Georgian capital, the studio aims to celebrate the site's industrial heritage. The Soviet-era locomotive factory will be renovated with some of its architectural features rebuilt with a contemporary spin. The new buildings will be connected by a network of tree-lined pedestrian public spaces, featuring apartments on upper levels and shops, cafes, and workshops on the ground floors. Brick finishes in blue-grey, terracotta, green, taupe, and white, chosen following colour mapping research in Tbilisi, will give each building its own identity. Featuring vaulted, sawtooth, and pitched roofs reminiscent of traditional industrial buildings, the structures will include planted terraced roofs alongside greenhouses and communal spaces, set within a landscape of sports facilities, parks, and boulevards.

articles.originalTitle: How Material Choices Shape Contemporary Additions to Historic Buildings - ArchDaily
articles.title: Material Selection and the Varna Approach for Contemporary Additions to Historic Buildings
articles.excerpt: Adding contemporary floors to historic buildings requires careful material selection to establish a relationship with the existing structure. The LH Residence project in Varna demonstrates how fiber cement panels can facilitate this architectural integration.
articles.content: Adding new floors on top of a historic structure presents challenges beyond accommodating additional space, raising questions about how contemporary interventions can respond to existing architectural character. Material selection plays a vital role in establishing relationships between different construction periods. The LH Residence in Varna, Bulgaria, exemplifies how fiber cement helps relate a contemporary addition to a historic building. Located in the historic center, the residence retains a two-story structure dating from 1923 and integrates it into a five-story composition. The original facade features limestone ornamentation and sculptural details by local artist Kiril Shivarov. To ensure the addition respects the historic architecture, the designers utilized a minimal grid and set the cladding slightly back. The suspended cladding system incorporates two distinct Swisspearl finishes on the new facades, while roof surfaces feature custom-colored panels matching the light tone of the original plaster. Although lacking formal protected-monument status, the original structure and decorative facade were preserved and restored, avoiding demolition and accommodating residential spaces alongside a ground-floor café.

articles.originalTitle: Arup creates arrow-shaped viewpoint for Fehmarnbelt Tunnel project - Dezeen
articles.title: Arup Creates Arrow-Shaped Viewpoint for Fehmarnbelt Tunnel Project
articles.excerpt: Engineering firm Arup has designed the demountable Pilen viewpoint in Denmark to allow the public to view the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel construction and understand its scale.
articles.content: Engineering firm Arup has designed a demountable viewpoint named Pilen in Denmark to offer the public views of the ongoing construction of the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel. Meaning "the arrow" in Danish, the structure overlooks the site of the 18-kilometre-long road-and-rail tunnel being built between Denmark and Germany. The ramped structure measures 217 metres in length, reflecting the exact size of each of the 89 individual concrete elements that will form the tunnel. Project architect Kristian Winther stated that the arrow-shaped design points toward the location where the tunnel emerges in Germany, acting as a compass needle for visitors. Commissioned by contractors Femern, Pilen is built from landfill timber and steel, and engineered to be demounted and reused once construction concludes in 2029. A fully accessible landscaped walkway zigzags as it rises 24 metres above sea level. The overall tunnel project is scheduled for completion in 2029, with expectations to reduce train journey times between Hamburg and Copenhagen to 2.5 hours.

articles.originalTitle: stars return to frank lloyd wright’s only built planetarium after twenty years - Designboom
articles.title: Frank Lloyd Wright's Planetarium Reopens After More Than Two Decades
articles.excerpt: The Miller Planetarium at Florida Southern College, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright, reopened to the public on September 26, 2026, following an extensive restoration.
articles.content: Located on the Florida Southern College campus, the Miller Planetarium designed by Frank Lloyd Wright reopened on September 26, 2026, after regular star shows had been suspended for more than two decades. Led by Jeff Baker of MCWB Architects, the restoration returned the 1950s building to its original circular seating arrangement alongside a new digital projection system. Exterior work addressed years of water damage, requiring the replacement of more than 280 hand-cast textile blocks using 3D-printed molds. Discoveries behind the facade during construction also allowed the team to introduce insulation to previously exposed areas. Inside, a computer closet from the 1980s was removed to restore Wright's original curved plywood benches into two concentric rings around the projection equipment. Floor finishes were restored to Cherokee Red, and wall colors were updated to a lighter scheme based on the original design. The final phase introduced a COSM digital projection system and a Bowen sound system, allowing the historic facility to resume educational presentations and astronomical programs for visitors.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: DeMellier Opens Its First Store in London’s Sloane Square, Designed to Feel Like a Stylish Home - WWD
articles.title: DeMellier Opens Its First Store in London's Sloane Square
articles.excerpt: Luxury handbag brand DeMellier is opening its first stand-alone store in London's Sloane Square ahead of its 10th anniversary, featuring interior design by Nicolas Schuybroek.
articles.content: Luxury handbag brand DeMellier is opening its first stand-alone store in Hugo Boss' former home on Sloane Square in London, ahead of its 10th anniversary next year. Founder Mireia Llusia-Lindh tapped residential architect Nicolas Schuybroek to create an interior that feels like a stylish home. Opening on Saturday, the 3230-square-foot space spans two floors. The ground level resembles a living room, while the downstairs features a dining room concept and a craft corner. Llusia-Lindh stated that the flagship gives customers the opportunity to step inside the brand world and experience its collections and craftsmanship in person. The London-based company closed its financial year at the end of July with 56 million pounds in revenue and is profitable. Online sales account for 80 percent of the business, with the rest distributed through partners including Galeries Lafayette, Neiman Marcus, Net-a-porter, Selfridges and Mytheresa. The brand utilizes leathers that are food chain byproducts, never destroys unsold pieces, and reuses or donates leftover materials to local apprentice schools. Through its A Bag, A Life initiative, a portion of every sale is donated to SOS Children’s Villages to fund vaccines and medical treatments for children in need.

articles.originalTitle: Collecting to Shape and Reflect the Nation Conference (In-person) - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum to Host Conference on National Identity and Museums
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum and the Germanisches Nationalmuseum are organizing a joint conference from October 22 to 24, 2026, examining national collections and identities.
articles.content: Organized jointly by the Victoria and Albert Museum and the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, the conference titled 'Collecting to Shape and Reflect the Nation' will take place from October 22 to 24, 2026, at V&A South Kensington in London. The multi-faceted event explores how national museum collections have assembled and shaped national identities from the nineteenth to the twentieth century. International scholars and museum professionals will participate in five panels addressing imperial legacies, postcolonial collections, restitution debates, and the construction of national identities through art collections. Tickets for the in-person event range from £35 to £45, with sales closing at 14.00 BST on Wednesday, October 21, 2026. An online version of the conference is also available for £25, offering remote access to the same academic sessions.

articles.originalTitle: Our ‘Design Directory’ 2026: The architects, studios and designers to know around the world - Monocle
articles.title: Global Design Industry and Architectural Landscape Highlighted in International Directory
articles.excerpt: Monocle magazine's new design directory compiles European architects, studios and designers who combine local craftsmanship and regional vernaculars with innovative solutions to shape global industry standards.
articles.content: The global design industry continues to expand with a new international directory celebrating the firms, studios and individuals at the top of their craft. Europe's architectural and design landscape draws upon a rich history ranging from ancient structures to modernist masterpieces, with contemporary practitioners utilizing these foundations for adaptive reuse and circular economies. In Austria, architectural practices integrate regional timber-building traditions and exacting craftsmanship, alongside civic projects like Vienna's hybrid timber market hall. Belgium's modern design scene features climate-conscious landscape architecture and mixed-use urban blocks. Czechia stands out for its adaptive reuse initiatives and community-minded civic infrastructure. Denmark maintains its leadership in functional minimalism through material-focused interiors and utilitarian objects, while Finland celebrates natural materials and human-centred design. France combines haute-couture craftsmanship with technological innovations to produce sculptural interiors, sustainable architecture and cinematic spaces. Germany's contemporary scene leads in efficient architecture and regional material usage, anchored by Berlin studios focusing on community capacity and human scale. Greece blends classical antiquity with modern regionalism across large-scale developments. Together, these international practitioners shape global standards by honouring local vernaculars.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Beverly Buchanan - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 to Feature Works by Beverly Buchanan
articles.excerpt: The Central Pavilion at the Venice Biennale hosts an exhibition of drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks by artist Beverly Buchanan, exploring Southern building traditions, land ownership, and custodianship histories.
articles.content: The 2026 edition of the Venice Biennale presents the artistic practice of Beverly Buchanan, who was born in Fuquay, USA, in 1940 and died in Ann Arbor in 2015. Hosted at the Central Pavilion, the presentation encompasses drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks by the artist. Buchanan's practice engages with histories of custodianship, land ownership, and architectural vernaculars, specifically through the prism of Black Southern building traditions. After earning master's degrees in parasitology and public health at Columbia University and exhibiting in New York City, Buchanan returned to the American South in 1977, living in Georgia before relocating to Michigan in 2010. The exhibition emphasizes the artist's voice as constructed through her writing, research notes, and fieldwork. Her short accompanying texts combine biography and invention to gather testimonies from individuals within and around her community. Utilizing diverse materials ranging from thrifted timbers and metals to medical spatulas, bottle caps, and concrete admixtures, Buchanan acknowledged the historical and social relativity of each medium. Her shack sculptures enact cultural preservation as a method, commemorating figures such as self-taught architect Mary Lou Furcron and artist Nellie Mae Rowe. Furthermore, her concrete and tabby works—incorporating oyster shells, water, sand, and ash—invoke the material economy and historical consciousness of coastal Georgia's survival.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Issa Samb - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Features Installations Dedicated to Issa Samb
articles.excerpt: The 2026 edition of Biennale Arte presents installations inspired by the Dakar courtyard of Senegallist artist Issa Samb, highlighting his multidisciplinary practice and grassroots artistic philosophy.
articles.content: Born in Dakar in 1945 and passing away there in 2017, Senegallist artist Issa Samb is featured in the Central Pavilion and Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026. Hailing from the Lebou community of sanctuary keepers, Samb worked across painting, collage, assemblage, sculpture, performance, and writing. He co-founded the Laboratoire Agit'Art collective with filmmaker Djibril Diop Mambéty and others, championing a grassroots, autonomous approach focused on public engagement rather than conventional cultural politics. His presence at the 2026 Biennale is articulated through installations inspired by his central Dakar home and courtyard, La Cour, which historically served as a meeting place for artistic and political thought. The presentation features costumes, suspended objects, assemblages, notes, and sketches. Additionally, a video contribution by Adrienne Edwards documents a visit to La Cour, while Ican Ramageli's film Cap Vers l’Est portrays Samb exploring liminal spaces where the living meets the dead. The exhibition runs from May through November.

articles.originalTitle: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1B in Total Costs - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Barack Obama Presidential Center Campus Costs Reach $1 Billion in Chicago
articles.excerpt: The total campus cost for the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Chicago has reached $1 billion, according to the non-profit Obama Foundation's latest filing, significantly exceeding the original $350 million estimate for the Jackson Park museum project.
articles.content: The complete campus of the Barack Obama Presidential Center on Chicago's South Side is projected to cost $1 billion. According to the latest filing from the non-profit Obama Foundation, the updated cost projection is about $91 million higher than the September figure of $909 million, excluding $123 million in publicly financed infrastructure improvements. Lakeside Alliance served as the joint venture contractor that completed the main campus building earlier this year. Foundation representatives stated that the recent increases stemmed from additional construction scope, including work on the 60,000-sq-ft Home Court basketball center, public art, and insurance. The Home Court facility was constructed under a separate contract by Elevate Design Builders Group, a joint venture of Bowa Construction and AECOM Hunt Construction. While the foundation reported no outstanding disputed charges with Lakeside Alliance, trade contractors noted they had not been informed whether the latest cost increases would address pending legal actions and liens against the project. The original project budget started at $350 million, grew to $500 million in 2017, and rose to $850 million in early September before reaching the current projection.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the collectors | Laurent Dumas - Art Basel
articles.title: New Contemporary Art Center Le Large Opens in Boulogne-Billancourt
articles.excerpt: Emerige real estate group opens Le Large in Boulogne-Billancourt, launching its inaugural contemporary art exhibition titled Moteur Imaginaire.
articles.content: A new contemporary art center dedicated to showcasing excellence, Le Large, opens on the western edge of Greater Paris in Boulogne-Billancourt. Established by the real estate group Emerige, the center focuses particularly on artists living and working in France. For its inaugural exhibition, titled Moteur Imaginaire, the venue explores the history of Île Seguin, which served as a major manufacturing site for the French car manufacturer Renault until its closure in 1992. Italian curator Cecilia Alemani has brought together around 60 artists for the exhibition, including Neïl Beloufa, Bianca Bondi, Théo Mercier, Jean-Luc Moulène, and Laure Prouvost. The exhibition aims to present the carmaker's art collection, which is rarely exhibited in France, to a broader public, examining the evolution of machines and human interaction. The inaugural exhibition runs from 17 October 2026 to 7 March 2027. Additionally, Laurent Dumas will participate in related conversation events as part of seasonal cultural programmes.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026: performances, lectures, discussions, roundtables - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Announces Performance and Public Programme
articles.excerpt: The final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition in Venice will feature a public programme of performances, lectures, debates, and roundtables at the Arsenale.
articles.content: The final ten days of the 61st International Art Exhibition, titled In Minor Keys, will run from 13 to 22 November at the Arsenale in Venice. The spaces will host a public programme of performances, lectures, debates, and roundtables, alongside an Assembly bringing together ten artist-led organisations and collectives. The lineup features performances by artists including Laurie Anderson, Ziad Antar, rana elnemr, Natalia Lassalle-Morillo and Sofiá Gallisá Muriente, Clarissa Herbst, Tammy Nguyen, Hagar Ophir, Yo-E Ryou, Dominique Rust, Lerato Shadi, and Nathalie Vairac. The Assembly serves as a platform to share ideas and creative practices, reflecting on pedagogy, research, and the tending of land, body, and community. Participating organisations operate across diverse geographies with varying sustainability models, united by their roles for cultural practitioners. The schedule includes a lecture by Felwine Sarr focusing on relationality and mobility, repeat performances of Tammy Nguyen's aria-based work, and a roundtable addressing the legacies of departed artists such as Issa Samb, Beverly Buchanan, Nancy Brooks Brody, Seyni Awa Camara, and Pauline Oliveros.
